title: Chapter 9: WB State Government & Political Structure

blocks.content: The Calcutta High Court, established in 1862 under the High Courts Act of 1861, remains the oldest High Court in India with jurisdiction extending over West Bengal and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: West Bengal currently operates with a unicameral legislature consisting of the West Bengal Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha).
The West Bengal Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) was officially abolished in 1969.
Calcutta High Court is the oldest High Court in India, holding jurisdiction over West Bengal and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
The Governor acts as the constitutional head of the state, while real executive authority resides with the Chief Minister and the Council of Ministers.
The state administrative secretariat functioning as the primary seat of executive power is located at Nabanna in Howrah.
Abolition of Vidhan Parishad: West Bengal abolished its Legislative Council in 1969 under Article 169 of the Constitution.
Calcutta High Court Jurisdiction: Frequently tested question on its dual territorial jurisdiction over West Bengal and Andaman & Nicobar Islands.
Constitutional Articles: Articles 153 to 167 in Part VI of the Indian Constitution deal with the State Executive.

cells: [EXAM TIP] Calcutta High Court (est. 1862) is the oldest High Court in India — even older than Allahabad HC. This is a key differentiator asked in WB exams.
